script: I walked 45km drunk, and what I found in Yeppoon stunned me.. I was 18 and drunk, so I crashed into the next town for a block party that was basically a crime fest. Cars were flying, people were high, and I was just there to drink. One of the drunk drivers asked if I wanted to ride home, but I was already buzzed enough, so I said I'd just crash at the bus stop. They told me the bus wouldn't run on Anzac Day because it was a holiday. I had $25, a busted phone, and the urge to stay alive. I could sleep in a bush and wait for the next day, but I'd be starving and homeless, and I didn't even know if the bus would still run. So I decided to walk. I hit every 24‑hour petrol station on the edge of town and grabbed supplies: two bottles of water, a Powerade, a Maximus, Doritos, Burger Rings, Twisties, a roll of duct tape, and scissors. I'd just watched Mythbusters use duct tape to build a rope, so I twisted it into a makeshift rope, a bandolier for my snacks, a holster for the Maximus, and a pouch for the scissors. I felt like a survivalist. By the time I left town, I'd walked an hour. The sky was overcast and dark; the highway was a black line. I kept going because I'd already walked that far. My phone died after an hour out of town, so I had no music or GPS. The sun was rising, cars were passing, and after about five hours my heels were blistered. I considered finding a bush to sleep, but the sky was still gloomy, and I didn't want to get soaked. I kept walking until the sun was high, and I realized the bus was gone. I was standing on the side of the highway, covered in duct tape, and I knew I'd spent my last dollar on Doritos. I ripped the tape off and left it behind—no point in carrying useless stuff. I had no money for the bus, so I kept going. After roughly 12 hours, I finally reached home. I collapsed into bed and slept for what felt like 18 hours. The next three days were a blur: I could barely stand, so I used a wheeled office chair to move around my unit and microwave food. I didn't drink much after that, but I still get into trouble when I am low on sanity. So yeah, I got drunk, walked 45 km, and learned that if you're a stupid 18‑year‑old with no money and a dead phone, you can either die or survive by walking. The moral? Don't let a drunk party ruin your life.
